description.narrative: UNICEF's "Armed Violence"-programme focusses on land mines and small and light weapons. The programme aims att reducing threats of armed violence, the spread of weapons and unexploded ordinances of war. This implementation includes strenthening national systems for protection of children and enhancing government's responsibilities.

UNICEF:s "Armed Violence"-program innefattar arbete med minor och små- och lätta vapen. Programmet ämnar minska hoten från väpnat våld, vapenspridning och explosiva lämningar av krig. Det görs genom att stäkra nationella system för skydd av barn och främja nationella regeringars ansvarstagande.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: Through the supported programme Unicef has strengthened child protection systems to address and reduce armed violence and increase protection of children from armed violence in Belize, Bosnia and Hercegovina, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua and Panamá. National ownership is important in Unicef's approach to sustainability, and different approaches were developed in different countries. For example, in Honduras Unicef advocacy and technical support contributed to harmonizing national legislation with the approval of Comprehensive Reform in Child and Family Matters, an adoption of a National Policy to Prevent Violence involving Children and Youth, the creation of the National Office for the Prevention of Violence and the Development of the Law for Carrying, Ownership and Use of Firearms and Explosives (the latter still in progress). In Nicaragua the programme has successfully prevented youth from being recruited into youth gangs and supported former gang members to be reintegrated into society. In Guatemala, the programme selected the 11 departments with the highest rates of violence against children, including armed violence, to implement a model of care and therapeutical assistance for child victims of armed violence and by organizing and training Committees against Child Abuse installed in national hospitals. There is also a mine and ERW (Explosive Remnants of War) awareness component of the programme, and this part of the programme has been carried out by Unicef with Sida support in DRC, Eritrea, Nepal, Pakistan, State of Palestine, Sri Lanka and Somalia. The focus is on mine and ERW risk education, especially among children. The programme also supports hospitals and health centres to better monitor mine injuries in order to provide basis for more effective strategies to prevent and reduce injuries.
